'''Travis James Wear''' (born September 21, 1990)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Travis Wear Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/weartr01.html|access-date=2020-11-08|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He began his pro career with the [[New York Knicks]] after going [[List of National Basketball Association undrafted players|undrafted]] in [[2014 NBA draft|2014]].

Wear was an [[All-American]] in high school and won a silver medal with United States U-18 national team at the [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]] in 2008. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] and the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. After playing one season with the Knicks, Wear played with [[San Sebastián Gipuzkoa BC]] in Spain for a year before returning to the U.S. to play with the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]].

==High school career==
Wear attended [[Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)|Mater Dei High School]] in [[Santa Ana, California]] where he was a two-time [[California Interscholastic Federation]] State champion in 2007 and 2008. As a junior, he averaged 16.1 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 8.3 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game. As a senior, he averaged 14.9 points and 6.4 rebounds per game.<ref name=bio>{{cite news |title=#24 Travis Wear |url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=207913828 |work=uclabruins.com |accessdate=September 5, 2014 |archive-date=September 2, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140902174609/http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=207913828 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Wear was listed as the No. 17 power forward and the No. 60 player in the nation in 2009.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Travis-Wear-55283;_ylt=AvaZNMV4mjT8WFOYo04twldGPZB4 Travis Wear Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==

===North Carolina===
Wear and his twin brother, [[David Wear|David]], played for the defending national champion [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] in their freshman year.<ref name=foster_030422014>{{cite news|last=Foster|first=Chris|title=UCLA's twin Wear brothers near the end of their identical act|date=March 2, 2014|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://articles.latimes.com/2014/mar/02/sports/la-sp-ucla-wear-twins-20140302|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140910195230/http://articles.latimes.com/2014/mar/02/sports/la-sp-ucla-wear-twins-20140302|archive-date=September 10, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Wear contributed 3.5 points and 2.2 rebounds a game while averaging over 10 minutes per game.<ref name=markazi/> The Tar Heels missed the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) tournament]], which upset their fans. Wear said playing for North Carolina "wasn't what [he] thought it would be."<ref name=foster_030422014/> The twin brothers transferred after the season in May 2010 to UCLA.  They [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] the following season due to NCAA transfer rules.<ref name=markazi>{{cite news |last1=Markazi |first1=Arash |last2=Leung |first2=Diamond |title=Wear twins transferring to UCLA |date=May 25, 2010 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/news/story?id=5219398 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100528224532/http://sports.espn.go.com/los-angeles/news/story?id=5219398 |archive-date=May 28, 2010 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===UCLA===
[[File:Travis Wear vs USC.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Wear against [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] in 2012]]
In his first season playing for UCLA in [[2011–12 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2011–12]], Wear played in 30 games with 24 starts, and averaged 26.2 minutes per game and finished second on the team in points per game (11.5) and rebounds per game (5.9). He had a career-high 13 rebounds in a loss against [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] on February 5, 2012. In [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13]], he started in 31 of his 32 games, and averaged 10.9 points and 5.2 rebounds in 28.9 minutes. He scored a career-high 23 points in a win at [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] on January 12, 2013.<ref name=bio/> UCLA won the [[Pac-12 Conference]] championship that season. However, UCLA coach [[Ben Howland]] was fired after the season, prompting Wear and his brother to consider transferring. After meeting with incoming coach [[Steve Alford]], the brothers were convinced they fit as starters in the new coach's system.<ref name=foster_030422014/>

Wear missed the first three games of [[2013–14 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2013–14]] after he had an [[appendectomy]] on October 28, 2013. He came off the bench in his first six games before returning to the starting lineup. He was ninth in the Pac-12 in [[field goal percentage]] (53.0), and shot 44% on [[three-point field goal]]s—including 10 of 19 in his final 16 games. He scored a season-high 16 points on 8-for-8 shooting in UCLA's win over [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] in the [[2014 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]] semifinals.<ref name=bio/> At the team's annual banquet at the end of the season, Wear was presented with the Elvin C. Ducky Drake Memorial Award as the team member who exhibits tremendous competitive spirit, inspiration and unselfish contributions. He graduated after the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=UCLA Looks Forward to Thursday Evening's NBA Draft|date=June 24, 2014|work=uclabruins.com|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=209529910|accessdate=June 27, 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===New York Knicks (2014–2015)===
[[File:LeBron James vs Travis Wear.jpg|thumb|upright|right|Wear defending [[LeBron James]] in 2014]]
Wear thought he had a chance to be selected in the second round of the [[2014 NBA draft]], but he went undrafted.<ref name=berman>{{cite news|last=Berman|first=Marc|title=Travis Wear came out of nowhere to win final Knicks roster spot|date=October 27, 2014|newspaper=New York Post|url=https://nypost.com/2014/10/27/travis-wear-came-out-of-nowhere-to-win-final-knicks-roster-spot/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028015506/http://nypost.com/2014/10/27/travis-wear-came-out-of-nowhere-to-win-final-knicks-roster-spot/|archivedate=October 28, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> He played for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[2014 NBA Summer League]],<ref>[http://www.nba.com/hawks/2014-atlanta-hawks-summer-league-roster 2014 Atlanta Hawks Summer League Roster]</ref> and was signed by the [[New York Knicks]] on September 9, 2014.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-sign-langston-galloway-and-travis-wear Knicks Sign Langston Galloway and Travis Wear]</ref> The Knicks' roster already had 15 players with guaranteed contracts, and Wear was a longshot to make the team.<ref name=berman/> However, they opened a roster spot for Wear by trading [[Travis Outlaw]]. Knicks president [[Phil Jackson]] said Wear was "overshadowed at UCLA but has the skill set to play every position from 1 to 4." He added that the team planned to have Wear play in the [[NBA Development League]], "where his possible NBA future solely depends on his ability to learn how to defend."<ref>{{cite news|last=Stein|first=Marc|title=Knicks send Travis Outlaw to 76ers|date=October 27, 2014|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/11774681/new-york-knicks-trade-travis-outlaw-philadelphis-76ers-clear-roster-room-travis-wear|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028073903/http://espn.go.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/11774681/new-york-knicks-trade-travis-outlaw-philadelphis-76ers-clear-roster-room-travis-wear|archive-date=October 28, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> The Knicks lost their [[2014–15 New York Knicks season|2014–15]] season opener in a 104–80 blowout to the [[Chicago Bulls]], but Wear made his pro debut in the fourth quarter with the game already decided.<ref>{{cite news|last=Berman|first=Marc|title=Knicks 'not ready for showtime' in opening rout by Bulls|date=October 29, 2014|newspaper=New York Post|url=https://nypost.com/2014/10/29/knicks-begin-new-era-getting-blasted-by-bulls/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141101233342/http://nypost.com/2014/10/29/knicks-begin-new-era-getting-blasted-by-bulls/|archivedate=November 1, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> The following night against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], he played 13 minutes in a 95–90 win, and held [[LeBron James]] to 0-for-4 shooting when he was the primary defender on James.<ref>{{cite news|title=Stats to know: Unhappy return for James|date=October 30, 2014|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/statsinfo/post/_/id/98015/stats-to-know-unhappy-return-for-james|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031100219/http://espn.go.com/blog/statsinfo/post/_/id/98015/stats-to-know-unhappy-return-for-james|archive-date=October 31, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

On January 8, 2015, Wear scored a season-high 21 points in a 120–96 loss to [[Houston Rockets]]. On March 22, 2015, he left the game against the [[Toronto Raptors]] with lower back soreness.<ref name=injury>{{cite web|last1=Rotowire|title=Travis Wear (back) is not playing Monday, Newsday reports.|url=https://www.thescore.com/nba/news/729122|website=thescore|date=23 March 2015 |accessdate=24 March 2015}}</ref> He missed the final 12 games of the season with the injury. He finished his rookie season averaging 3.9 points and 2.1 rebounds in 51 games.<ref name="miss season finale">{{cite web|last1=Wise|first1=Brandon|title=Knicks forward Travis Wear to miss season finale Wednesday|url=http://fantasynews.cbssports.com/fantasybasketball/update/25150611/knicks-forward-travis-wear-to-miss-season-finale-wednesday|website=CBSSports.com|date=15 April 2015 |publisher=CBSSports|accessdate=15 April 2015}}</ref>

=== Gipuzkoa Basket (2015–2016) ===
On October 7, 2015, Wear signed with [[Gipuzkoa Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite web|title=TRAVIS WEAR SE SUMA AL JUEGO INTERIOR DEL RETABET.ES GBC|url=http://www.gipuzkoabasket.com/noticias/travis-wear-se-suma-al-juego-interior-del-retabetes-gbc-N3071.php|work=GipuzkoaBasket.com|date=October 7, 2015|accessdate=October 7, 2015|language=Spanish}}</ref> In 26 games, he averaged 7.5 points, 4.2 rebounds and 0.7 blocks in 20.5 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/euro/players/travis-wear-1.html|title=Travis Wear Europe Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|accessdate=October 12, 2016}}</ref>

===Los Angeles D-Fenders / South Bay Lakers (2016–2018)===
On September 1, 2016, Wear signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Lakers Sign Julian Jacobs and Travis Wear|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/160901jacobswearsigned|accessdate=September 1, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=September 1, 2016}}</ref> but was waived on October 12 after appearing in two preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/161012-roster-update|title=Lakers Waive Auguste, Jacobs, Wear|work=NBA.com|date=October 12, 2016|accessdate=October 12, 2016}}</ref> He played 2016–17 with the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Lakers,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/161030-d-fenders-finalize-training-camp-roster/|title=D-Fenders Finalize Training Camp Roster and Schedule|work=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2016|accessdate=November 2, 2016|archive-date=March 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170305002523/http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/161030-d-fenders-finalize-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and averaged 12.7 points and 7.3 rebounds per game.<ref name=oram_10122017/>

Wear played with the Lakers in the [[2017 NBA Summer League|2017 summer league]], and again joined the NBA team for their training camp.<ref name=oram_10122017>{{cite news|last=Oram|first=Bill|title=Lakers get Lonzo Ball and his 'special skill' back in practice|date=October 12, 2017|newspaper=Orange County Register|url=http://www.ocregister.com/2017/10/12/lakers-get-lonzo-ball-and-his-special-skill-back-in-practice/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014062325/http://www.ocregister.com/2017/10/12/lakers-get-lonzo-ball-and-his-special-skill-back-in-practice/|archivedate=October 14, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

Wear spent most of the season with the NBA G League [[South Bay Lakers]].

=== Los Angeles Lakers (2018) ===
Wear signed a 10-day contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on March 2, 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lakers Sign Travis Wear|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180302-lakers-sign-travis-wear|date=March 2, 2018|work=NBA.com|accessdate=March 2, 2018}}</ref> Two days later, he made his Los Angeles debut against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], playing the entire fourth quarter and scoring seven points with two rebounds to help the team rally to a 116–112 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975686|title=Ball, Randle rally Lakers past Spurs late, 116-112|work=ESPN.com|date=March 4, 2018|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> After his second 10-day contract expired later that month,<ref>{{cite news|title=Lakers sign Travis Wear to a second 10-day contract|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/usa/nba/267810/lakers-sign-travis-wear-to-a-second-10-day-contract.html|date=March 13, 2018|work=Sportando.basketball|accessdate=March 13, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> Wear signed a deal for the remainder of the season<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Travis Wear for the Rest of the Season|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180323-lakers-sign-travis-wear|website=NBA.com|accessdate=March 23, 2018|date=March 23, 2018|language=en}}</ref> and was assigned twice to South Bay. During the offseason, the Lakers signed Wear to a [[two-way contract]] for 2018–19.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lakers Sign Travis Wear to a Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180724-lakers-sign-travis-wear |website=NBA.com |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |date=July 24, 2018}}</ref> However, they waived him after the first game of the season to sign forward [[Johnathan Williams]] to a two-way deal.<ref>{{cite news|last=Turner|first=Broderick|title=LeBron James has made Lakers' ticket prices higher than the Warriors'|date=October 19, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-report-20181019-story.html|accessdate=October 20, 2018}}</ref>

===Return to South Bay (2018–2020)===
On November 27, 2018, the [[South Bay Lakers]] announced they had acquired Wear as a returning player.<ref>{{cite news|first=Noah|last=Camarena|title=South Bay Lakers acquire Travis Wear|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-travis-wear/|date=November 27, 2018|work=NBA.com|accessdate=November 27, 2018}}</ref> In January 2020, he suffered a season-ending injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=South Bay Lakers Acquire Pierre Jackson|date=January 17, 2020|website=NBA.com|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-pierre-jackson/|accessdate=September 1, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Wear is the son of David Sr. and Gloria Wear. His father played college basketball at [[Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball|Fresno State]] and [[Cal State Fullerton Titans men's basketball|Cal State Fullerton]] and professionally overseas.<ref name="bio" /> Wear's favorite basketball player of all time is [[Magic Johnson|Earvin "Magic" Johnson]]. His twin brother, [[David Wear|David]] also became a professional basketball player.
